message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering the last 24 hours ending 2026-07-15 05:10 IST. New relevant findings were confirmed for SonicWall SMA 1000, Microsoft Windows Server/AD FS, Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop, Microsoft July security updates, and Ubuntu package security notices.

**Finding 1: SonicWall SMA 1000 Series multiple vulnerabilities**

- Product: SonicWall / Dell SonicWall SMA 1000 Series
- Issue: CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410 / SNWLID-2026-0008
- Severity: Critical for CVE-2026-15409 (CVSS 10.0); High for CVE-2026-15410 (CVSS 7.2)
- Description: SonicWall reports a server-side request forgery issue and a remote code execution issue affecting SMA 1000 Series 12.4.3 and 12.5.0 firmware branches. SonicWall says these vulnerabilities are confirmed as actively exploited in the wild.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes SonicWall and Dell SonicWall. SMA 1000 is a SonicWall secure access product, so this maps directly to the monitored product family.
- Source: SonicWall product notice, published and updated July 14, 2026: https://www.sonicwall.com/support/notices/product-notice-sma-1000-series-affected-by-multiple-vulnerabilities/kA1VN000001nv6D0AQ

**Finding 2: Microsoft AD FS DKM container ACL hardening**

- Product: Windows Server 2012 R2 / Windows Server AD FS
- Issue: CVE-2026-56155
- Severity: Important, per Microsoft/Cisco Talos reporting; exploited in the wild per Microsoft/Talos reporting
- Description: Microsoft documents an AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL issue where overly permissive permissions may expose key material used to protect token-signing and token-encryption private keys. The July 14 Windows security update starts audit-mode hardening and opt-in remediation.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Windows Server 2012 R2. Microsoft says the hardening applies to Windows Server 2012 ESU and Windows Server 2012 R2 ESU, among later Windows Server versions.
- Source: Microsoft Support KB5121391: https://support.microsoft.com/servicing/os/windows/docs/2026/07/kb5121391-cve-2026-56155-ad-fs-dkm-container-acl-hardening

**Finding 3: Google Chrome Stable Channel security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: Chrome 150.0.7871.124/.125 security update; includes CVE-2026-15764, CVE-2026-15765, CVE-2026-15766, CVE-2026-15767 and additional fixes
- Severity: Includes Critical and High issues as stated by Google
- Description: Google released Chrome Stable updates for Windows, Mac, and Linux on July 14, with 15 security fixes. The listed issues include critical use-after-free flaws in Ozone and high-severity memory-safety issues in Skia/libyuv.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Google Chrome.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases, July 14, 2026: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/

**Finding 4: Mozilla Firefox 152.0.6 security update**

- Product: Mozilla Firefox
- Issue: MFSA 2026-67 / CVE-2026-15718
- Severity: Critical
- Description: Mozilla announced Firefox 152.0.6 on July 14 to fix a critical invalid-pointer vulnerability in the JavaScript/WebAssembly component. Mozilla says exploit code is public but that it is not aware of attacks in the wild abusing the flaw.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Mozilla Firefox.
- Source: Mozilla MFSA 2026-67: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-67/

**Finding 5: Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop Application security update**

- Product: Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop Application
- Issue: APSB26-77 / CVE-2026-48272 and CVE-2026-48344
- Severity: Critical, CVSS 7.8
- Description: Adobe released a Windows Creative Cloud Desktop update fixing two critical privilege-escalation vulnerabilities. Adobe states it is not aware of exploitation in the wild for the issues addressed.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Adobe Creative Cloud.
- Source: Adobe APSB26-77, published July 14, 2026: https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/creative-cloud/apsb26-77.html

**Finding 6: Microsoft July 2026 security update batch**

- Product: Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Edge, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Defender and related Microsoft components
- Issue: July 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, including 622 vulnerabilities per Cisco Talos and Microsoft-derived reporting
- Severity: Mixed; Cisco Talos reports 57 marked Critical by Microsoft, including critical RCE issues in Windows services, Office applications, SQL Server, Defender, and other components
- Description: Microsoft released a large July security update set on July 14. Cisco Talos notes two exploited vulnerabilities this month, plus many critical RCE issues across monitored Microsoft product families.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows 10, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Edge, MSSQL, Microsoft .NET, PowerShell, Windows Defender, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, TFS / Azure DevOps, and Azure AD Connect.
- Source: Cisco Talos Microsoft Patch Tuesday review, July 14, 2026: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/microsoft-patch-tuesday-july-2026/

**Finding 7: Ubuntu security notices for July 14**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: Multiple Ubuntu Security Notices, including USN-8543-1 Wget, USN-8542-1 Dnsmasq, USN-8526-2 libheif, USN-8541-1 Vim, USN-8540-1 OpenVPN, USN-8539-1 GnuTLS, USN-8538-1 alsa-lib, USN-8537-1 httplib2, and USN-8536-1 MariaDB
- Severity: Not consistently stated in the listing; individual notices should be reviewed for package-level severity and affected releases
- Description: Canonical published multiple Ubuntu security notices on July 14 covering supported Ubuntu releases and fixing several CVEs across common OS packages.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices listing: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Possible matches needing review**

**Microsoft Edge Chromium fixes**

- Microsoft Edge is in Products.txt. Microsoft’s Edge security release notes for July 14 say Microsoft is aware of recent Chromium security fixes and is actively working on a security fix. Because that wording does not confirm an Edge release was available in the checked window, I did not count it as a confirmed patched Edge finding.
- Source: Microsoft Edge security release notes: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Fortinet / FortiOS**

- Products.txt includes Fortigate/FortiOS. Fortinet PSIRT search results surfaced July 14 FortiOS-related advisories, including FG-IR-26-154 and FG-IR-26-152, but the detailed FortiGuard advisory page could not be reliably retrieved during this run. Treat this as a review item rather than a confirmed digest finding until the Fortinet advisory details are verified directly.
- Source: Fortinet PSIRT listing/search result: https://www.fortiguard.com/psirt

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for the actively exploited SonicWall SMA 1000 vulnerabilities and Microsoft AD FS/Windows Server exposure. Browser and desktop software findings should be handled through standard accelerated patch channels because the Chrome and Firefox releases include critical vulnerabilities.
